'''Naum Zuselevich Shor''' ({{langx|ru|Наум Зуселевич Шор}}) (1 January 1937 – 26 February 2006) was a [[USSR|Soviet]] and [[Ukrainians|Ukrainian]]  [[mathematician]] specializing in [[optimization (mathematics)|optimization]].

He made significant contributions to [[nonlinear programming|nonlinear]] and [[stochastic programming]], numerical techniques for [[subgradient method|non-smooth optimization]], [[discrete optimization]] problems, [[semidefinite programming|matrix optimization]], [[Lagrange duality|dual quadratic bounds]] in [[Multiobjective optimization|multi-extremal programming]] problems.

Shor became a full member of the [[National Academy of Science of Ukraine]] in 1998.

==Subgradient methods==
{{Main|Subgradient method}} 
{{See also|Ellipsoid method|Linear programming|Convex optimization|Computational complexity theory|Iterative method}}

N. Z. Shor is well known for his [[iterative method|method]] of [[subgradient|generalized]] [[gradient descent]] with [[Quasi-Newton method|space dilation]] in the direction of the difference of two successive [[subgradient]]s (the so-called r-algorithm), that was created in collaboration with Nikolay G. Zhurbenko.<ref>N. Z. Shor and N. G. Zhurbenko, "The minimization method using space dilatation in direction of difference of two sequential gradients," Kibernetika, No. 3, 51-59 (1971).</ref><ref>
Free implementations of r-algorithm (made by workers of Department Methods for solving complex optimization problems led for a long time by N. Z. Shor) are available in 

* [http://imsc.uni-graz.at/kuntsevich/solvopt/ SolvOpt]
* [http://openopt.org/ralg ralg] from [[OpenOpt|OpenOpt framework]].</ref> The [[ellipsoid method]] was re-invigorated by A.S. Nemirovsky and D.B. Yudin, who developed a careful [[Analysis of algorithms|complexity analysis]] of its [[approximation algorithm|approximation]] properties for problems of [[convex minimization]] with real data. However, it was [[Leonid Khachiyan]] who provided the rational-arithmetic complexity analysis, using an [[ellipsoid method|ellipsoid]] '''[[algorithm]]''', that established that [[linear programming]] problems can be solved in polynomial time.

It has long been known that the ellipsoidal methods are special cases of these subgradient-type methods.

== R-algorithm ==
Shor's '''r-algorithm''' is for unconstrained minimization of (possibly) non-smooth functions,<ref>N.Z. Shor. ''Minimization Methods for Non-differentiable Functions''. Springer-Verlag, New York, 1985.</ref> which has been somewhat popular despite an unknown [[Rate of convergence|convergence rate]].<ref>"The Speed of Shor's R-Algorithm", available at http://www.optimization-online.org/DB_HTML/2007/05/1656.html</ref>  It can be viewed as a [[quasi-Newton method]], although it does not satisfy the secant equation.  Although the method involves [[Subderivative|subgradients]], it is distinct from his so-called ''subgradient method'' described above.
